tldr: Agentic Reasoning is a framework that enhances LLM reasoning by integrating three external agents—Web-Search, Code, and Mind-Map—enabling dynamic tool use during reasoning chains. Deployed on DeepSeek-R1, it achieves state-of-the-art results among public models, narrowly closing the gap to proprietary systems like OpenAI Deep Research.
contributions: Proposed Agentic Reasoning, a streamlined framework integrating external LLM-based agentic tools (web-search, coding, and Mind-Map agents) into reasoning processes
Explored Web-Search agent design, identifying a strategy combining query breakdown, reranking, RAG, and Mind-Map reasoning context that outperforms prior search/RAG approaches
Developed a knowledge-graph-based Mind-Map agent that constructs structured knowledge graphs for memory, improving coherence in long reasoning chains and handling complex logical relationships
Evaluated on expert-level benchmarks (Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA, GAIA) and deep research tasks, achieving new SOTA among public models and surpassing proprietary baselines like Gemini Deep Research
methods: The framework uses DeepSeek-R1 as the primary reasoning model, which dynamically embeds specialized tokens during reasoning to call external agents: a Web-Search agent (using Bing with Cohere Rerank 3.5, query breakdown via DeepSeek-V3, and threshold-based iterative refinement capped at three iterations), a Code agent (using Claude-3.5-Sonnet for code generation and Python 3.11 for execution), and a Mind-Map agent (using DeepSeek-V3 for knowledge graph construction and GraphRAG retrieval). The reasoning process temporarily halts when agent tokens are detected, dispatches queries with reasoning context from the Mind-Map, and reintegrates results back into the chain in an iterative retrieve-and-reason cycle.
results: Humanity's Last Exam: 23.8% accuracy with DeepSeek-R1, a +14.4% improvement over the base model's 9.4%, narrowing the gap to OpenAI Deep Research (26.6%) to just 2.8%
GPQA: achieved new SOTA among public models, surpassing OpenAI o3-mini-high and outperforming Search-O1 by approximately 5%
GAIA: established new SOTA among publicly available methods, surpassing OpenAI Deep Research on Level 1 (74.36% vs 74.29%) and Level 2 (69.21% vs 69.06%), with a 2.26% gap on Level 3
Deep research: consistently outperformed RAG, RAgent, Search-O1, STORM, and Gemini Deep Research across all benchmarks
Werewolf game: achieved 72% win rate with Mind-Map versus 36% without, significantly surpassing human expert performance
Tool ablation showed web search performed best among single tools, and combining all three tools yielded synergistic improvements exceeding the sum of individual gains
limitations: Adding more tools beyond the three selected agents often degrades performance due to increased risk of inappropriate tool selection
Many capabilities (e.g., translation, code interpretation) are already embedded within the reasoning model, making external integration redundant
Inaccuracies in external tool outputs can negatively affect overall response quality
Knowledge Refinement component was found redundant with Rerank and became ineffective when combined with other Web-Search components
Open-source approaches still trail proprietary models (e.g., 2.8% gap to OpenAI Deep Research on Humanity's Last Exam, which benefits from a stronger internal reasoning model)
OpenAI Deep Research experiments were restricted by a high paywall, limiting direct comparison
